reviewNotes: National Day 20 May, the motto (English: Peace, Work, Fatherland), and the English anthem title are well-known; check the exact wording with an official source. Colour meanings are intentionally left out.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Symbols
blocks.md: Our country has **symbols**. The **flag** has three stripes of green, red and yellow, with a yellow star on the red stripe. The **motto** is **Peace, Work, Fatherland**. The **national anthem** is **O Cameroon, Cradle of Our Forefathers** (in English).

blocks.caption: The flag of Cameroon.
blocks.alt: A flag with green, red and yellow stripes and a yellow star on the red stripe.

blocks.title: National Day
blocks.md: **National Day** is on **20 May**. On that day people march and celebrate in towns and villages. Pupils may take part in the parade. We stand and respect the flag and the anthem.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The flag has a yellow star, on the red stripe.
- The motto has three words: Peace, Work, Fatherland.
- Stand still when the anthem is played.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What are the three colours of the flag?
steps: Look at the flag from left to right.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: On which date is the National Day?
steps: It is in the month of May.

objectives: Say that Cameroon has ten regions.
Name some regions and their capitals.
reviewNotes: Regions and regional capitals are standard facts; check against the textbook.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Regions
blocks.md: Cameroon is divided into **ten regions**. Each region has a **capital town**. The capital of the country is Yaoundé, which is also the capital of the Centre Region.

blocks.caption: The ten regions and their capitals.
blocks.alt: Ten boxes with each region and its capital.

blocks.title: Some regions
blocks.md: Littoral: Douala. Centre: Yaoundé. West: Bafoussam. North-West: Bamenda. South-West: Buea. South: Ebolowa. East: Bertoua. Adamawa: Ngaoundéré. North: Garoua. Far North: Maroua.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not mix up Buea (South-West) and Bamenda (North-West).
- Douala is the biggest city, but Yaoundé is the capital.
- There are ten regions, not nine or eleven.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: What is the capital of the North-West Region?

blocks.title: Example 2
steps: Count the regions in the list.

lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level I (Class 2) — Social Studies; to be checked against the official texts
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Name food crops and cash crops.
reviewNotes: Where crops grow is stated in general terms. Check with the textbook for the main regions.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Food crops
blocks.md: **Food crops** feed families: **cassava**, **maize**, **plantain**, **yams**, **cocoyams**, **beans**, **groundnuts** and **rice**. People also eat fish, meat, eggs and many fruits like mangoes, pawpaw and oranges.

blocks.caption: Some crops of Cameroon.
blocks.alt: Six boxes with cassava, maize, cocoa, coffee, cotton, banana.

blocks.title: Cash crops
blocks.md: **Cash crops** are grown to sell. In Cameroon they include **cocoa**, **coffee**, **bananas**, **cotton**, **oil palm** and **rubber**. Cocoa and coffee are grown in the forest and highland areas. Cotton is grown mainly in the north.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Some crops are both food and cash crops.
- Not all crops grow in every region.
- Farmers need rain, soil and care.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Is cassava a food crop or a cash crop here?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Name a crop that is grown to sell.

lessons.title: Celebrations, respect and helping others

objectives: Name some celebrations and say how we respect each other.
Say how we can help people in need.
reviewNotes: List of celebrations is inclusive and not exhaustive; check with the school's context.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Celebrations
blocks.md: Families and communities have celebrations: **birthdays**, **weddings**, **harvest festivals**, **Christmas**, **Eid**, **National Day** and **Youth Day**. People wear nice clothes, share food, sing and dance. Cameroon has many cultures, and we respect them all.

blocks.caption: Respect and help.
blocks.alt: Four boxes about respect and help.

blocks.title: Helping others
blocks.md: We can **help** people who are old, ill, poor or new in our school. Share food, give your seat, carry a bag, and be a friend. Helping makes the community stronger. Say thank you for help.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Do not laugh at other people's culture or clothes.
- Do not take part in anything that is unsafe.
- Help with care: ask a trusted adult if the help is big.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: How can you help an old person who is carrying a heavy bag?
steps: Say: May I help you, please?

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: A new girl comes to your class. What do you do?
steps: Greet her and play with her.
